plan:
- Microcontroller: Raspberry Pi 4 B or equivalent for primary processing and display output, with dedicated drivers for all screens (IPS, E-Ink, round LCD).
- Power System: Custom PCB for power management, 50,000 mAh Li-Po battery pack, charge controller, DC-DC converters, and heavy-duty 5V input port. Status LED panel for charge indication.
- Mechanical Chassis: Weather-resistant Pelican-style case or custom 3D-printed modular chassis (carbon fiber composite or matte olive drab/black texture). Custom mounts for displays, radio, sensors, and control elements.
- Display & Control: 7-inch IPS LCD, 4.2-inch E-Ink display, 1.28-inch round LCD. Rotary encoder, waterproof toggle switches with safety covers.
- Sensors & Radios: Baofeng UV-5R radio integration, Beitian GPS antenna, BME280/BNO055 environmental/IMU sensors. RTL-SDR dongle with external antenna, integrated USB ports.
- Lighting & Peripherals: 3x high-power LEDs (White, UV, IR) with heatsink, various small indicator LEDs, robust wiring throughout.

originalPrompt:
Subject: A rugged, portable tactical survival computer ("Cyberdeck" style), designed for mountain and off-grid use.

Form Factor & Material: A hard-shell, weather-resistant pelican-style case or a custom 3D-printed modular chassis (carbon fiber or matte olive drab/black texture). It should look like military-grade field equipment. Dimensions are roughly the size of a thick tablet or a small netbook.

Primary Display (Inner Lid/Top Panel): A 7-inch IPS LCD screen (for Raspberry Pi), displaying a topographical map or an SDR (Software Defined Radio) waterfall interface.

Secondary Display (Bottom Panel/Control Deck): A 4.2-inch E-Ink (e-paper) screen, displaying clear, high-contrast GPS coordinates, altimeter data, and breadcrumb trails.

Tertiary Display (HUD): A small, round 1.28-inch LCD screen mounted near the top edge, displaying a digital compass rose and weather arrows.

Control Interface (Bottom Panel): A prominent, tactile rotary encoder knob (machined aluminum) with push-button functionality. A set of heavy-duty, waterproof toggle switches with safety covers (for power management).

Radio Integration: On the side or physically slotted into the chassis, the main body of a Baofeng UV-5R radio (antenna protruding from the top). Short, coiled patch cables connecting the radio's side jacks into the main chassis.

Sensors & Emitters: A protruding, domed GPS antenna module (Beitian). A small, protected window for BME280/BNO055 sensors. A cluster of 3 high-power LEDs (White, UV, IR) mounted on the front or side edge like a directional flashlight array, covered by a heat sink.

Power & Ports: Visible heavy-duty 5V power input ports. A status LED panel showing the charge of a massive 50,000 mAh internal battery. Exposed, ruggedized USB ports for plugging in the RTL-SDR dongle (with its small telescopic antenna attached).

Lighting/Atmosphere: Dramatic, utilitarian lighting. Rendered with high photorealism, emphasizing the varied textures: matte plastic, brushed metal knobs, glowing screens, and heavy-duty cabling. The E-ink screen must look distinctly like electronic paper (matte, no backlight), while the 7-inch screen is bright and vivid.

subSteps.title: Print core chassis components (base and lid)

detail.tip: To ensure maximum weather resistance and strength, consider drying your Carbon Fiber PETG filament before printing to prevent moisture-related print defects and choose a print orientation that minimizes visible layer lines on critical sealing surfaces.
steps: Prepare your 3D printer with a clean, leveled bed and load Carbon Fiber PETG filament (matte black or olive drab).
Print the Custom Modular Chassis Base (220x150x50mm) using Carbon Fiber PETG, ensuring high infill (>60%) and settings optimized for waterproof layer lines.
Print the Custom Modular Chassis Lid (220x150x25mm) with the same Carbon Fiber PETG material and high infill/waterproof settings.

After cooling, carefully remove both chassis components and thoroughly inspect for dimensional accuracy, layer adhesion, and any defects that could compromise weather resistance or structural integrity.
detail.summary: 3D print the robust cyberdeck chassis base and lid.

subSteps.title: Print modular chassis inserts (radio bay, port panel, control panel)

detail.tip: For a truly tactical look, ensure your PETG filament is a matte finish and consider matching the color to the Carbon Fiber PETG chassis, or using a contrasting dark color.
steps: Load PETG filament (matte olive drab recommended) into your 3D printer.
Print the Baofeng Radio Bay Insert (105x55x35mm) with medium infill and strong walls (e.g., 3-4 perimeters).
Print the External Port Panel Insert (100x50x20mm) using the same PETG settings.
Print the Control Deck Panel (120x60x10mm) with high infill (>60%) for extra sturdiness.
Inspect all printed inserts for fit, finish, and ensure all mounting points and cutouts are clear and accurate.
detail.summary: Print all modular chassis inserts for controls and peripherals.

subSteps.title: Print internal mounts and trays (RPI, battery, power boards)

detail.tip: For the battery tray, consider reinforcing critical stress points in your slicer software to ensure it can withstand the weight and potential vibrations of the large LiPo pack during rugged use.
steps: Load black PETG filament into your 3D printer.
Print the Raspberry Pi Mount (90x60x10mm) and Power Module Mount Plate (60x40x5mm) using standard PETG settings.
Print the LiPo Battery Tray (185x85x65mm) with medium infill (e.g., 40%) and strong walls (e.g., 3-4 perimeters) for robust battery retention.
Carefully remove all printed parts and verify their dimensions and fit against the corresponding electrical components.
detail.summary: Print internal mounts and trays for the RPi, battery, and power modules.

subSteps.title: Print display bezels and mounts

detail.tip: Ensure that the visible surfaces of the bezels are printed with a high-quality finish, as they will be prominent components of the cyberdeck's aesthetic.
steps: Load PETG filament (matte black or olive drab recommended) into your 3D printer.
Print the 7-inch LCD Bezel/Frame (170x110x5mm) with standard PETG settings.
Print the E-Ink Display Bezel/Frame (108x83x3mm) with standard PETG settings.
Print the Round HUD Display Mount (45x45x8mm) with standard PETG settings.
Inspect all printed bezels and mounts to ensure clean edges and accurate dimensions for optimal display fit and aesthetic integration.
detail.summary: Print bezels and mounts for all three displays.

subSteps.title: Print sensor and LED housings/shrouds

detail.tip: For optimal UV resistance and waterproofing on the GPS dome, consider applying a clear UV-resistant sealant or paint after printing.
steps: Load PETG filament (matte black or olive drab recommended) into your 3D printer.
Print the GPS Antenna Dome Shroud (30x30x20mm) with waterproof and UV-resistant settings to withstand outdoor exposure.
Print the LED Array Housing (45x25x20mm) with high infill and heat-resistant settings to support the multi-spectrum LED array and heatsink.
Print the RTL-SDR Antenna Mount (20x20x15mm) and Charge Status LED Panel Frame (50x25x3mm) using standard PETG settings.
Switch to Clear PETG filament and print the Sensor Window Frame (20x15x5mm) with standard settings.
Carefully inspect all printed parts for smooth finishes and accurate dimensions, especially the clear frame and heat-resistant housing.
detail.summary: Print all remaining sensor, LED, and status indicator housings.

subSteps.title: Cut and fit the chassis sealing gasket

detail.tip: Pre-fitting the gasket without adhesive can help identify any areas that require trimming or adjustment for a perfect seal. Use a contact adhesive or marine-grade sealant for best waterproof results.
steps: Measure the perimeter of the Custom Modular Chassis Base's sealing channel.
Carefully cut the EPDM Foam Gasket (600x10x3mm) to the measured length, ensuring clean, straight cuts for optimal sealing.
Apply a thin, even bead of high-strength, waterproof adhesive along the sealing channel of the chassis base.
Press the custom-cut EPDM Foam Gasket firmly into the adhesive-lined channel, ensuring no gaps or overlaps at the corners.
Allow the adhesive to fully cure according to the manufacturer's instructions, ensuring a robust and weather-resistant seal.
detail.summary: Cut and fit the custom EPDM foam gasket for chassis sealing.

subSteps.title: Cut and fit the sensor protective window

detail.tip: When working with acrylic, use masking tape along your cut lines to prevent chipping and ensure a cleaner break. For optimal clarity, clean the window with a microfiber cloth before final adhesive application.
steps: Carefully measure the internal dimensions of the Sensor Window Frame (20x15x5mm) opening.
Using a sharp acrylic cutting tool or a fine-tooth saw, cut a piece of 2mm thick Acrylic Sheet to the measured dimensions (approximately 15x10mm).
Deburr and smooth all edges of the cut acrylic piece with fine-grit sandpaper to ensure a clean finish and prevent snags.
Test fit the cut acrylic window into the Sensor Window Frame to ensure a snug, flush fit. Trim as necessary for a perfect seal.
Apply a small bead of clear, waterproof adhesive (e.g., silicone or epoxy) around the inner perimeter of the frame and carefully press the acrylic window into place.
detail.summary: Cut and fit the acrylic protective window for the environmental sensors.

subSteps.title: Wire the external power input, charge controller, and main battery pack
Wire main power toggle and 5V DC-DC converter from battery
Connect 5V power bus to Raspberry Pi and ruggedized USB hub
Wire Raspberry Pi GPIO to E-Ink display, round LCD, and rotary encoder
Connect Raspberry Pi to GPS, environmental, and IMU sensors via UART/I2C
Wire LED array power toggle and connect to multi-spectrum LED array
Connect USB hub to Raspberry Pi and prepare external USB connections
Prepare audio interface for Baofeng radio integration
Install Raspberry Pi OS and basic drivers
Test 7-inch IPS LCD display via HDMI
Verify E-Ink and round LCD functionality with SPI drivers
Test rotary encoder and switch input responsiveness
Confirm GPS, BME280, and BNO055 sensor data acquisition
Test high-power LED array illumination and control
Verify battery charge status panel and charging input
Test RTL-SDR dongle and Baofeng audio interface connectivity
Mount the Raspberry Pi and internal power boards
Install the main LiPo battery pack into its tray
Mount primary 7-inch LCD into lid chassis with bezel
Integrate E-Ink and round HUD displays into chassis base and lid
Install rotary encoder, knob, toggle switches, and safety covers onto control panel
Mount Baofeng radio into its bay insert
Install external port panel with power input, USB hub, and LED array
Mount GPS module, environmental/IMU sensors, and status LED panel
Route all internal wiring, secure with cable ties, and fasten chassis lid

projectDescription: A rugged, thick tablet-sized cyberdeck for off-grid survival, featuring a Raspberry Pi, 7-inch IPS and 4.2-inch E-Ink displays for maps and sensor data. It integrates a Baofeng radio, GPS, environmental sensors, and multi-spectrum LED array within a weather-resistant, custom 3D-printed chassis, all powered by a high-capacity LiPo battery.

tools: 3D printer (PETG and Carbon Fiber PETG capable)
M2 and M3 hex key set
Adhesive or hot glue gun (for securing wires)
assumptions: Basic knowledge of 3D printing and post-processing techniques.
Familiarity with Raspberry Pi OS installation and basic configuration.
Basic electronics knowledge including GPIO, SPI, I2C, and UART protocols.
Competency in basic soldering techniques for PCBs and wire connections.
